guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: Updating FY’26 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA; reaffirming cash from operations outlook.

desk.headline: Revenue down 4% to $607m, a touch below estimates; adjusted EPS $0.10 beat; FY26 revenue and EBITDA outlook cut
results: Revenue fell 4% to $607m, mainly because the cost of the new Italy Lotto licence is now taken off revenue ($99m this quarter vs $53m).
Underlying growth drivers added about 4%: product sales more than doubled to $60m and other service revenue rose 11%.
US multi-state jackpot revenue dropped 30% against a strong year-ago comparison; Italy revenue fell 19%.
Adjusted EBITDA slipped 2% to $289m but the margin improved to 47.5%; adjusted EPS fell to $0.10 from $0.36, largely due to the licence amortization.
Over $200m went to dividends and buybacks this year to 9 November; net debt rose to $3.8bn after the final Italy Lotto payment.

guidance.summary: Brightstar cut its 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges, citing weaker second-half same-store sales, slower Italy consumer expansion and a weaker euro. Its cash-from-operations outlook was kept, and capex was trimmed.

items.metric: Cash from operations (excl. Italy Lotto payment)

points: The CFO blamed the cut on an Italian summer heat wave and transport strikes, softer US jackpot play and a stronger dollar, which drove most of the EBITDA change.
Management expects Q4 growth from underlying drivers to stay in the mid-single digits, led by product sales, but with a lower margin mix.
A draft Italian budget law would extend the Lotto licence by 15 months to end-2029 for about €188m; it still needs parliament's approval.
Bids for the Texas and New York lottery contracts remain open; management said it expects to compete strongly for both.
The company said capital returns stay a key priority and leverage remains within its target range; a refreshed medium-term outlook is planned for early 2027.
call.source: Earnings call transcript (Earnings Whispers, 10 Nov 2026); CEO and CFO comments in the results release
